title: The reflex arc
objective: Trace the components of a reflex arc from receptor to effector.

steps.title: The unit of physiology
steps.body: A **[[reflex arc]]** is the shortest sense-and-respond circuit: a **receptor** → an **[[afferent]]** (sensory) neuron → integration in the CNS → an **[[efferent]]** (motor) neuron → an **[[effector]]** (muscle or gland). The knee-jerk is the classic monosynaptic example.

visual.alt: Knee-jerk reflex: a hammer taps the patellar tendon and a muscle spindle in the quadriceps fires. The signal runs up the afferent (sensory) fibre, past its pseudounipolar cell body in the DRG, into the dorsal spinal cord and straight onto a motor neuron in the ventral horn through a single synapse. The motor neuron fires, the efferent (motor) axon carries the command to the quadriceps, and the muscle contracts. The animation ends with the lower leg kicked forward.
visual.caption: Receptor, afferent, one synapse in the cord, efferent, effector: the shortest sense-and-respond loop.

steps.prompt: Order the components of a reflex arc.
items: Afferent neuron carries it to the CNS
Efferent neuron carries the command out
steps.explanation: Receptor → afferent → CNS → efferent → effector. Some reflexes are monosynaptic (one synapse); most add interneurons.

steps.prompt: In the knee-jerk reflex, what are the afferent and efferent limbs?
options: Afferent: a stretch sensor in; efferent: a motor neuron out to the muscle
Afferent: a motor neuron in; efferent: a stretch sensor out
Afferent: a pain fiber in; efferent: a motor neuron out to the muscle
Afferent: a stretch sensor in; efferent: an interneuron out to the muscle
steps.explanation: A muscle-stretch receptor sends the afferent signal; a motor neuron forms the efferent limb back to the muscle, which contracts.

variants.setup: A tendon tap stretches the muscle and it contracts.
variants.prompt: Which limb carries the 'stretch detected' signal inward?
variants.reveal: The afferent limb carries the sensory signal in; the efferent limb drives the contraction out.

steps.title: Why the arc matters
steps.body: Much of physiology is built from reflex arcs, stacked and modulated — somatic (knee-jerk), autonomic (pupil, bladder), and interoceptive. Identify the receptor, the limbs, and the effector, and you can read almost any circuit.

steps.prompt: Label the structures of this spinal reflex arc.
steps.explanation: A muscle spindle's afferent (cell body in the DRG) synapses on a motor neuron that contracts the quadriceps.

reviewNotes: Reflex arc components; foundation for autonomic/interoceptive reflexes.
